content: Dapsone, also known as 4,4'-diaminodiphenylsulfone (DDS), is primarily utilized as a treatment for Dermatitis herpetiformis, a chronic blistering skin condition associated with celiac disease. It is also an antibacterial agent used in the management of susceptible cases of leprosy, a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae. Dapsone appears as a white, odorless crystalline powder. It is practically insoluble in water and completely insoluble in fixed and vegetable oils, which limits its solubility in certain formulations. This medication is available by prescription and is provided in oral tablet form, with dosages of 25 mg and 100 mg. The inactive ingredients in Dapsone tablets include colloidal silicon dioxide, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and corn starch, which serve as excipients to aid in the manufacturing process and stability of the drug.
